title: THE INTRODUCTION
hook: After two years together, I am introduced as his friend. His mother is paying our rent.

evidenceFacts.claim: At my first family dinner, his mother introduced me to a neighbor as “his friend.”
We had been together for two years and were adults.
My partner heard the introduction and kept setting the table.
His mother paid our rent while I looked for work.
The neighbor smiled at me and waited.
I stood by the table, could speak within their hearing, and could correct the introduction or let it pass.
I wanted recognition and feared risking rent help; withdrawal and the mother’s reason were unknown.

tension.protect: Public recognition of an established relationship, and the housing help we depend on.
tension.description: One ordinary introduction asks me to decide whether to name a relationship in front of someone who materially supports us.

poles.motive: Be introduced as the partner I am, within my partner’s hearing.
Avoid risking rent help in an unfamiliar family setting.

tension.ethicalAsymmetry: Misnaming the relationship is not made equally legitimate by financial support. Letting it pass is understandable under dependence, without endorsing erasure. Correcting is not promised to be safe or celebrated.
tension.whyNow: The introduction concerns me, and the neighbor is waiting for me. I can speak for my own relationship; I cannot make my partner speak.
tension.power: The mother controls current financial assistance; the source gives no explicit threat. The partner is present and heard it, but his motive becomes available only in reveal.
unknowns: What my partner was thinking then.
Whether correcting would change rent assistance.
Whether the family already recognized the relationship elsewhere.

scenes.entryState: I am at my first dinner with this family, in an established two-year relationship, materially dependent on rent help.

arc.change: The mother introduces me as “his friend.” My partner keeps setting the table within hearing; the neighbor waits for my response.
arc.understanding: Recognition and dependence are present at once. I do not know whether the wording is intentional or what correction would cost.
arc.nextSceneReason: Only my accepted response can lead to the author encounter; there is no next room or informational quest.
arc.removalLoss: The single frame is the whole opportunity. Removing it leaves text, which is a valid competing format.

scenes.exitState: One of two acts accepted; neighbor smile remains the sourced entry expression without changing.

opportunities.motive: Make the relationship visible in my partner’s hearing.
opportunities.physicalEnactment: Hero turns toward the neighbor and begins a small speaking gesture; caption: “You say you are his partner.” No synthetic dialogue.
opportunities.confirmationCopy: Say to the neighbor that I am his partner, within their hearing? Your version ends as you say it.
opportunities.finalPose: Hero facing neighbor, hand relaxed near body; partner still setting table in the held reconstruction.
opportunities.stopFrame: Hero speaking intention delivered before any change in mother, partner or neighbor.

opportunities.label: Let this introduction pass
opportunities.motive: Avoid a public correction while depending on rent assistance.
opportunities.physicalEnactment: Hero stays by table in a neutral pose; caption: “You let this introduction pass without correcting it.” No nod or friendly agreement invented.
opportunities.confirmationCopy: Let this introduction pass without correcting it? Silence will be recorded only because you confirm.
opportunities.finalPose: Hero at original mark, unspeaking; neighbor retains existing smile.
